Bangladesh wage board meets as garment worker protests continue | The Straits Times
Bangladesh wage board meets as garment worker protests continue
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
A demonstrator hurls back a tear gas shell fired by police following a clash between the police and garment workers protesting for higher wages, in Narayanganj, Bangladesh, November 4, 2026. REUTERS/Abdul Goni
Published Nov 04, 2026, 04:22 PM
Updated Nov 04, 2026, 04:22 PM
DHAKA, Nov 4 - Bangladesh's newly formed wage board is set to hold its first meeting on garment sector wages on Wednesday, as protests for higher pay entered their fifth day.
The government and garment manufacturers are under mounting pressure to raise the monthly minimum wage to 30,000 taka ($243) from 12,500 taka, as workers struggle with rising living costs.
The protesters have clashed with police in several industrial areas of Dhaka, forcing hundreds of factories to suspend operations and raising concerns about shipment delays in Bangladesh, the world's second-largest garment exporter after China.
The sector employs about 4 million workers, generates more than 80% of export earnings and supplies brands including H&M , Inditex's Zara and Walmart .
On Wednesday, clashes broke out between workers and police in Savar and Gazipur, two major garment hubs on the outskirts of Dhaka. Demonstrators blocked roads and highways, while police used tear gas and sound grenades. Several factories suspended operations amid concerns over further unrest.
The six-member wage board, which includes representatives of workers and factory owners, is expected to begin formal discussions on reviewing the industry's wage structure.
Workers said the existing minimum wage was no longer sufficient to meet basic household expenses after years of rising food, housing and other living costs.
"Every month is a struggle," said Bithi Begum, a garment worker. "After working hard all day, the money we earn is hardly enough to cover even our basic needs."
International buyers are closely watching the situation as factories enter a key production period for spring and summer orders.
Swedish fashion retailer H&M told Reuters that some factories had closed temporarily, though it had not experienced major supply-chain disruptions.
Manufacturers said the industry was already under pressure from rising costs, stronger regional competition, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in the Middle East and weaker demand in key export markets.
Experts said the wage board faced the challenge of balancing workers' demands with the competitiveness of a sector that is central to Bangladesh's economy.
Selim Raihan, an economics professor at the University of Dhaka, said Bangladesh could absorb a significant wage increase without necessarily losing its competitive advantage if factories improved productivity.
He said any wage revision should also reflect inflation, living costs and factories' ability to pay, while international buyers should help support improved labour standards through fairer purchasing practices and prices.
Raihan said prolonged labour unrest could pose a greater threat to the industry than higher wages because it undermines delivery reliability and buyer confidence.
"Treating cheap labour as the industry's permanent competitive strategy would be a mistake," he said. "Bangladesh needs to move increasingly toward productivity, reliability, upgrading and higher-value products." REUTERS

中国在北京与伊朗、阿曼和沙特官员举行会议，并敦促重返谈判。外交部长王毅呼吁保护航道和“理性精神”。

北京—中国11月4日表示，避免中东重新陷入敌对状态是其与该地区国家外交努力的“首要任务”。
在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周末对伊朗发出新的战争威胁后，北京最近几天加大力度解决这场长达八个月的危机。
北京外交部发言人毛宁在11月4日的新闻发布会上表示：“当务之急是避免中东地区重新爆发敌对行动，给该地区人民带来灾难。”
她补充说，北京将“支持伊朗和美国通过谈判解决争端，推动也门问题政治解决，帮助就霍尔木兹海峡开放问题达成妥善、全面的解决方案”。
作为伊朗的最大经济伙伴，中国于11月2日在北京连续与伊朗、阿曼和沙特官员举行会议，敦促重返谈判桌。
外交部长王毅在与沙特国家安全顾问穆萨德·本·穆罕默德·艾班和伊朗最高国家安全委员会副秘书阿里·巴盖里·卡尼分别会晤时呼吁保护航道，并敦促本着“理性精神”。
中国领导人习近平本周还在北京会见了阿曼苏丹，并警告中东不要成为“大国竞争的角力场”。
中国外交部发言人在新闻发布会上表示，11月晚些时候，北京将派遣中东特使前往伊朗、阿曼和沙特阿拉伯，作为“穿梭外交访问的一部分……旨在促进和平谈判并缓解紧张局势”。法新社

China says avoiding new hostilities in Middle East a ‘top priority’

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq after a signing ceremony at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Nov 2.

China says avoiding new fighting in the Middle East is a “top priority” after Donald Trump threatened Iran. Beijing wants Iran and the US to talk and to ease tensions in Yemen and the Strait of Hormuz.
China held meetings with Iranian, Omani and Saudi officials in Beijing and urged a return to negotiations. Foreign Minister Wang Yi called for protected shipping lanes and a “spirit of reason”.
Xi Jinping warned the region must not become a “wrestling ground for major-country rivalry”. China will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in November for peace talks and tension relief.
BEIJING – China said on Nov 4 that avoiding a return to hostilities in the Middle East was a “top priority” in its diplomatic efforts with countries in the region.
Beijing has stepped up efforts in recent days to resolve the eight-month-long crisis after US President Donald Trump issued a fresh war threat against Iran over the weekend.
“The top priority is to avoid the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East that would bring disaster to the region’s people,” Beijing’s foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a news conference on Nov 4.
Beijing will “support Iran and the US in resolving disputes through negotiations, promote finding a political settlement to the Yemen issue, to help reach a proper and comprehensive solution for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz”, she added.
China, a top economic partner of Iran, hosted back-to-back meetings on Nov 2 with Iranian, Omani and Saudi officials in Beijing, urging a return to the negotiating table.
Foreign Minister Wang Yi called for shipping lanes to be protected and urged a “spirit of reason” in separate meetings with Saudi National Security Adviser Musaad bin Mohammad al-Aiban and Iran’s Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping also met Oman’s Sultan for talks in Beijing this week, where he warned against the Middle East becoming a “wrestling ground for major-country rivalry”.
Later in November, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as a part of “shuttle diplomacy visits... aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions”, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson told a news briefing. AFP

summary: 中国寻求从泰国引渡五名维吾尔人海峡时报 中国寻求从泰国引渡五名维吾尔人 立即注册：了解亚洲快速发展的发展 发布于 2026 年 11 月 4 日晚上 07:02 更新于 2026 年 11 月 4 日晚上 07:02 曼谷，11 月 4 日 - 泰国政府发言人表示，泰国将允许五名维吾尔男子在批准驱逐出境之前在法庭上质疑中国的引渡请求人权组织警告说，如果他们被遣返，他们将面临酷刑的风险。这些人是 300 名维吾尔人中的一员，维吾尔人是西部地区受迫害的少数民族，人口约 1000 万。
content:
中国寻求从泰国引渡五名维吾尔人海峡时报
中国寻求从泰国引渡五名维吾尔人
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
发表于 2026 年 11 月 4 日 07:02 PM
更新于 2026 年 11 月 4 日 07:02 PM
曼谷，11 月 4 日 - 泰国政府发言人表示，泰国将允许五名维吾尔男子在法庭上质疑中国的引渡请求，然后再批准将他们驱逐出境。人权组织警告说，如果他们被遣返，他们将面临酷刑的风险。
这些人是 300 名维吾尔人中的一员，维吾尔人是西部新疆地区遭受迫害的少数民族，人口约 1000 万，他们于 2014 年逃往东南亚国家，并因非法入境而被拘留。
这五名维吾尔人后来因越狱而被起诉。政府发言人 Ekkapob Pianpises 周三告诉路透社，其中两人目前已接近刑期满。
埃卡波布说：“泰国政府已授予他们对此案提出异议的权利。”他补充说，这两人已被任命为律师，法院将决定他们的异议。
国家安全委员会秘书长猜亚普鲁克·杜昂普拉帕特 (Chaiyapruek Duangprapat) 将军周三对记者表示，另外三人仍需因企图越狱而在泰国监狱再待一年。
2014年，中国西部新疆地区发生一波暴力袭击事件，引发中国当局大规模镇压，数百甚至数千名维吾尔人逃离了骚乱。人权组织和联合国指责北京虐待维吾尔少数民族，包括在拘留营中大规模使用强迫劳动。北京否认有任何侵权行为。
在被问及引渡五名维吾尔人的请求时，中国外交部发言人毛宁告诉记者，中泰两国在打击偷渡等跨境犯罪方面的合作符合两国法律、国际法和惯例。
泰国和中国于 1993 年签署了引渡条约，并于 1999 年生效，但根据该条约提出的请求必须通过泰国法院。
人权组织敦促泰国停止引渡，称这些人在中国面临酷刑和其他虐待的严重风险。
人权观察组织亚洲部主任伊莱恩·皮尔森（Elaine Pearson）表示：“前泰国政府多年来一直对维吾尔人进行不人道的拘留，然后按照北京的要求将他们送往中国，并在那里强迫他们失踪。”
泰国于次年将 2014 年被捕的近 100 名维吾尔人遣返回中国，引起广泛谴责，同时有 170 多人被确认为土耳其公民并被送往土耳其。
一些外交官和安全分析人士将这次驱逐与一个月后造成 20 人死亡的曼谷圣地爆炸事件联系起来。
随后，泰国于 2025 年 2 月将同一群体中的另外 40 名维吾尔人驱逐到中国，尽管联合国人权专家呼吁停止遣返他们。路透社

China seeks extradition of five Uyghurs from Thailand | The Straits Times
China seeks extradition of five Uyghurs from Thailand
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Published Nov 04, 2026, 07:02 PM
Updated Nov 04, 2026, 07:02 PM
BANGKOK, Nov 4 - Thailand will allow five Uyghur men to challenge a Chinese extradition request in court before approving their deportation, a Thai government spokesman said, with human rights groups warning they face the risk of torture if sent back.
The men were among 300 Uyghurs, a persecuted minority numbering around 10 million in the western region of Xinjiang, who fled to the Southeast Asian country in 2014, where they were detained for illegal entry.
The five Uyghurs were later prosecuted for escaping detention. Two are now near completing their sentences, government spokesperson Ekkapob Pianpises told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The Thai government has granted them the right to contest the case," Ekkapob said, adding the two men had been appointed a lawyer and the courts would decide their challenge.
The three others still have to spend another year in Thai jail for their escape attempt, General Chaiyapruek Duangprapat, secretary-general of the National Security Council, told reporters on Wednesday.
Hundreds, possibly thousands, of Uyghurs fled unrest in China's western Xinjiang region in 2014, following a wave of violent attacks that prompted a massive crackdown by Chinese authorities. Rights groups and the UN have accused Beijing of abuses against the Uyghur minority, including the mass use of forced labour in internment camps. Beijing denies any abuses.
Asked about the extradition request of the five Uyghurs, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters that China and Thailand's cooperation in tackling cross-border crimes such as human smuggling was in line with both countries' laws, international law and practice.
Thailand and China signed an extradition treaty in 1993 that entered into force in 1999, but requests under the pact must go through Thai courts.
Human rights groups urged Thailand to halt the extradition, saying the men faced a grave risk of torture and other abuses in China.
"Previous Thai governments have kept Uyghurs in inhumane detention for years and then complied with Beijing's demands to send them to China, where they were forcibly disappeared," said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch.
Thailand sent nearly 100 of the Uyghurs arrested in 2014 back to China the following year, drawing widespread condemnation, while a group of more than 170 were identified as Turkish citizens and sent to Turkey.
Some diplomats and security analysts have linked that deportation to the bombing of a Bangkok shrine a month later that killed 20 people.
Thailand then deported another 40 Uyghurs from the same group to China in February 2025 despite appeals from United Nations human rights experts to halt their return. REUTERS

title: 德州翻藍：民主黨時隔38年首奪聯邦參議員席次
summary: Author, 加里·奧多諾霍（Gary O'Donoghue） Author, 布蘭登·德雷農（Brandon Drenon） 民主黨人詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）贏得德克薩斯州（Texas；得州）關鍵的參議員選舉，被視為今次美國中期選舉的最大爆冷之一。 他擊敗共和黨對手肯·帕克斯頓（Ken Paxton），是1988年以來首次有民主黨人在德州贏得聯邦參議員席位。這場勝利不僅改寫德州數十年來的政治版圖，也進一步鞏固民主黨對美國國會的控制。 塔拉里科是教師
content:
Author, 加里·奧多諾霍（Gary O'Donoghue）
Author, 布蘭登·德雷農（Brandon Drenon）
民主黨人詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）贏得德克薩斯州（Texas；得州）關鍵的參議員選舉，被視為今次美國中期選舉的最大爆冷之一。
他擊敗共和黨對手肯·帕克斯頓（Ken Paxton），是1988年以來首次有民主黨人在德州贏得聯邦參議員席位。這場勝利不僅改寫德州數十年來的政治版圖，也進一步鞏固民主黨對美國國會的控制。
塔拉里科是教師出身，直到去年之前都鮮為人知。他將共和黨執政下生活成本上升作為競選主軸，爭取選民支持。
共和黨的帕克斯頓則曾多次與特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）同台造勢，並將塔拉里科描繪成對德州而言過於進步的候選人。

在德州首府奧斯汀的一場觀票派對上，當電視宣布塔拉里科勝選時，他的支持者陷入狂歡。
他們擁抱、親吻、舉杯慶祝。許多人說，自己不敢相信這會實現。
塔拉里科在附近一間表演藝術中心的正式觀票派對上登台，現場掌聲雷動。他宣布：「我們剛剛奪回了德州。」
「我們證明了，再多的金錢也比不上德州人民的力量。」
這是指他擊敗了共和黨對手帕克斯頓，而帕克斯頓的競選活動獲全球首富馬斯克（Elon Musk）的支持。
他競選期間常用宗教語言，把自己的勝算渺茫，比作《聖經》中「大衛戰勝歌利亞」的故事。
他說：「這場勝利，是獻給每一位曾經懷疑是否有人在聆聽的德州人。我聽見你們了，我們聽見你們了。今晚，全世界都聽見你們了。」
Play video, "為何美國中期選舉對特朗普至關重要？", 節目全長 8,18
數十年來，對德州的自由派來說，民主黨人贏得全州性選舉，一直像是白日夢。
德州是美國人口第二多的州，一直是保守主義的堡壘，經常推行日後被其他地方效法的共和黨政策。
但在整個競選期間，民調顯示身為州議員的塔拉里科，逐漸突破傳統政治版圖，激勵了急切渴望新領導層的德州民主黨基本盤。
選戰開支也隨之大幅飆升，很快成為美國聯邦參議員選舉史上最昂貴的一場，花費超過5億美元（36億元人民幣；150億元新台幣）。
馬斯克向支持共和黨帕克斯頓的超級政治行動委員會（Super PAC），注資1.58億美元，而這也成為塔拉里科攻擊對手的重要素材。
更令人意外的是，以德州作為政治根據地的共和黨政治世家布什家族（Bush family；布希／布殊），竟有兩名成員公開支持塔拉里科，此舉被視為帕克斯頓敗選的預兆。
喬治華盛頓大學（George Washington University）政治學教授夸德里科斯·德里斯克爾（Prof Quardricos Driskell）向BBC表示，帕克斯頓是共和黨失敗的主要原因之一，稱他是「客觀而言糟糕的候選人」。
他說，塔拉里科在德州的勝利，加上週二（11月3日）另一場爆冷，擊敗了該州共和黨籍州長阿博特（Greg Abbott），「絕對是歷史性的」。阿博特落敗，也意味著民主黨自1990年代以來首次贏得德州州長選舉。
德里斯克爾教授談到民主黨在這個「孤星之州」的收穫時說：「這不只是海嘯，不只是公投，而是一場血洗。⋯⋯這明確顯示，這個國家想走向不同的方向。」
塔拉里科在民主黨初選中，擊敗了知名對手、達拉斯國會議員賈絲敏·克羅基特（Jasmine Crockett）。
此後，儘管面對大量負面廣告攻擊，包括針對他過去支持跨性別者權益的言論，他的支持度仍維持穩定。
競選期間，他經常談及自己的宗教背景。他的祖父是一名南方浸信會（Southern Baptist）牧師，而他本人也曾在神學院學習，因此演說中經常引用《聖經》典故。
Play video, "The expensive battle to turn Texas blue", 節目全長 0,31
2023年，他被自己所屬政黨以貪腐指控彈劾，後來獲該州參議院宣判無罪。他也曾遭美國證券交易委員會（SEC）以聯邦詐欺罪名起訴，但案件後來被撤控。
特朗普則多次赴德州，替帕克斯頓及其他共和黨候選人站台，甚至前往原本穩定支持共和黨的地區舉辦造勢活動，顯示共和黨高層對投票率感到憂心。
選民對高昂的物價感到不滿，包括汽油價格，並將原因歸咎於特朗普的關稅政策及對伊朗戰爭。
此外，美墨邊境地區及拉丁裔選民亦對特朗普移民政策感到不滿。
儘管特朗普執政下非法越境人數大幅下降，而這一直是德州選民重視的議題，但民調顯示，特朗普在拉丁裔選民中的支持度明顯流失。
拉丁裔約佔德州總人口三分之一。自夏末以來的多項調查顯示，多數德州拉丁裔選民如今不認同特朗普的施政，而許多人曾在2024年大選中轉而支持他。
多位在選前接受BBC訪問的德州拉丁裔選民表示，促使他們改變立場的重要原因之一，是特朗普強力打擊移民的政策。
他們提到，部分執法措施導致美國公民遭拘留，非暴力犯罪者也被大規模逮捕，讓許多人感到不安。

content:
美國中期選舉2026：民主黨歷史性勝利 深入共和黨票倉攻城掠地——BBC記者澤克爾觀察 - BBC News 中文
Author, 安東尼·澤克爾（Anthony Zurcher）
民主黨改寫了唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）的政治版圖，而這個夜晚所帶來的衝擊波，未來多年都將震撼美國政壇。
隨着民主黨在一連串數十年來穩定支持共和黨的州份贏得重要參議院勝利，其中堪薩斯州更是近一個世紀以來首次出現這種情況，一股藍色巨浪席捲全國，將共和黨逐出權力中心。
在特朗普總統第二個任期過半之際，民主黨如今已牢牢掌控眾議院，並重新奪回參議院多數席位。
他們將有能力阻撓特朗普的施政議程，並對其政府展開調查。史無前例的第三次彈劾嘗試也可能被提上日程。
在特朗普於2025年1月重返白宮，並在共和黨全面掌控國會的情況下執政後，幾乎沒有人能想像會出現這樣的結果。
隨着公眾輿論轉而反對他及其政黨，民主黨曾寄望重新奪回眾議院。
但面對一張看來對自己不利的參議院選舉版圖，他們原本認為前景艱難，因為其中許多州在兩年前都由特朗普輕鬆拿下。
然而，民主黨最終憑藉在德克薩斯州（Texas；得州）、緬因州、堪薩斯州、俄亥俄州、艾奧瓦州（Iowa；愛荷華／衣阿華）以及北卡羅來納州和南卡羅來納州的勝利，改寫了政治算式。
Play video, "為何美國中期選舉對特朗普至關重要？", 節目全長 8,18
在接受BBC美國合作夥伴哥倫比亞廣播公司（CBS）訪問時，特朗普承諾將與國會民主黨人達成協議，並表示自己不希望在任期最後兩年都花時間否決他們提出的法案。
不過，他稍後在「真相社交」（TRUTH Social）上發布了一張自己標誌性的紅色棒球帽照片，上面印有「veto」（否決）字樣，某程度上削弱了這番表態。
總統接着指出，今年的選票上沒有他的名字，但如果有的話，共和黨將取得壓倒性勝利。
然而，特朗普曾幫助許多共和黨候選人提升聲勢，並敦促選民將這次選舉視為他爭取連任。
在參議院方面，民主黨至少翻轉六個席位，輕鬆取得多數地位。
亞當·漢密爾頓（Adam Hamilton）在堪薩斯州勝出。該州上一次選出民主黨參議員還是在近100年前的大蕭條時期。
詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）在德州參議院選舉中擊敗共和黨人肯·帕克斯頓（Ken Paxton），終結民主黨在該州全州級選舉38年的連敗紀錄。
此文包含Instagram提供的内容。由於這些内容會使用曲奇或小甜餅等科技，我們在加載任何内容前會尋求您的認可。 您可能在給予許可前希望閲讀Instagram曲奇政策和隱私政策。希望閲讀上述内容，請點擊“接受並繼續”。
在南卡羅來納州，安妮·安德魯斯（Annie Andrews）擊敗達琳·格雷厄姆（Darline Graham），後者是在其兄長、參議員林賽·格雷厄姆（Lindsey Graham）去世後獲任命接替該席位。即使在幾個月前，也鮮有分析人士認為這個席位具有競爭性。
五度當選的共和黨參議員蘇珊·柯林斯（Susan Collins）承認在緬因州參議院選舉中敗給民主黨人特洛伊·傑克遜（Troy Jackson）。
殘奧運動員喬什·圖雷克（Josh Turek）奪下由即將退休的共和黨參議員喬妮·恩斯特（Joni Ernst）持有的艾奧瓦州參議院席位。民主黨也重新奪回俄亥俄州的參議院席位，由謝羅德·布朗（Sherrod Brown）在復出之戰中擊敗喬恩·赫斯特德（Jon Husted）。
與此同時，在密歇根州一場激烈角逐的參議院選舉中，民主黨人阿卜杜勒·埃爾—賽義德（Abdul El-Sayed）擊敗共和黨人邁克·羅傑斯（Mike Rogers）。
民主黨挑戰者吉娜·伊諾霍薩（Gina Hinojosa）擊敗現任共和黨州長格雷格·阿博特（Greg Abbott）。就在今年稍早，後者仍被視為穩操勝券。
民主黨同時贏得艾奧瓦州、俄亥俄州及佐治亞州的州長選舉。佐治亞州更創下歷史，選出首位黑人女性州長。
與此同時，民主黨自2022年以來首次贏得眾議院多數席位。
預計民主黨將贏得245個眾議院席位，共和黨則為166席。

民主黨翻轉了德州、北卡羅來納州、賓夕法尼亞州、艾奧瓦州、肯塔基州及科羅拉多州等地的眾議院席位，並準備在弗吉尼亞州及印第安納州擴大戰果。
南方各州的黑人民主黨選民以破紀錄人數投票，協助該黨取得勝利。而曾幫助特朗普在2024年贏得總統大選的拉丁裔選民，也明顯轉向支持民主黨。
民主黨贏得了德州與墨西哥邊境沿線三個以拉丁裔人口為主的國會選區全部眾議院席位。
在佛羅里達州，拉丁裔選民也幫助民主黨守住眾議院席位，挫敗州內共和黨透過重劃選區奪取席位的計劃。
事實上，去年數月以來主導新聞頭條的國會選區重劃之爭，最終對共和黨而言並未帶來成果。
在德州，他們原本希望透過重新劃線為本黨增加五個席位，但到星期二（11月3日），他們最終甚至可能失去一席。
如果說保守派還有一線希望，那就是整體而言佛羅里達州似乎仍偏向右翼。
共和黨參議員阿什莉·穆迪（Ashley Moody）以些微優勢成功連任，眾議員拜倫·唐納茲（Byron Donalds）也當選這個「陽光之州」首位黑人州長。
而陷入困境的共和黨人也成功保住佛蒙特州及新罕布什爾州州長職位。但這樣的亮點寥寥可數。
隨後，他便以此姿態施政，推動在貿易及移民議題上的部分不受歡迎政策，並發動一場遭多數美國民眾反對的對伊朗戰爭。
星期二，選民向他作出了沉重斥責，而這種教訓將不會輕易被遺忘。

When massive Yellow Vests protests were taking place in Paris, We Are Change was there reporting on the ground and risking safety as protesters were losing eyes due to police brutality. In the past we have also been to places likeSomalia, Venezuela and Cheran , once the most violent, dangerous area in Mexico.
As for Hong Kong, it’s very expensive to fly and stay there. This mission will involve spending a week or more investigating, reporting and live-streaming.
So if you value reporting on the events in Hong Kong that is independent and free of spin and manipulation, then your support is crucial! By contributing to this campaign, you will help fund the cost of the flight, safety precautions and live reporting at events like the upcoming Civil Human Rights Front March on August 31 and the student strike that is set to take place on September 2, the first day of secondary school.
Our $2,700 goal is the bare minimum it will take to fund this trip. If we surpass the goal due to your support, which is so greatly appreciated, the funds will go toward other journalistic endeavors. Thank you so much! Your support means the world to us!

content:
Fundraiser by tyrone thomas : Unite for Digital Fearlessness
tyrone thomas is organizing this fundraiser.
"Use what's in your hand" - Adam Clayton Powell Jr.
Your phone isn't just for posting stories and playing music. That little computer in your pocket has more power than entire governments had 20 years ago. Like the ancient Abhaya Mudra - the fearless hand gesture that banishes fear and offers protection from the "Evil Eye" - we're transforming these devices into something that helps communities meet the coming challenges with a sense of fearlessness, rooted in Free Collaboration and Privacy.
Abhaya started as disaster recovery - how do communities rebuild communication when the towers are down and the power's out? But we realized something profound: the same tools that help neighborhoods coordinate after a hurricane are exactly what we need when authoritarians try to silence us. Like the protective Abhaya Mudra, this system creates a shield against the "evil eye" of surveillance while becoming a helpful digital companion that guides and empowers our communities.
Drawing inspiration from Buckminster Fuller's vision of global cooperation for humanity's benefit, Abhaya is designed as the foundation for communities to work together toward a more equitable future. The ecosystem operates through five interconnected elements:
• Tor + Mobile based Mesh Networks: Messages that flow around censorship like water
• Mesh Based Distributed Storage: Truth that lives everywhere so it can't be destroyed
• Mesh Based Distributed Computation Service: AI-capable shared processing power for communities to solve their own challenges
• Sensor/Peripheral IO: User Controlled Eyes and ears embedded in the network
• Mesh Federation: Connecting local networks into unstoppable global resistance
"The ultimate measure of a man is not where he stands in moments of comfort and convenience, but where he stands at times of challenge and controversy." - MLK Jr.
After Hurricane Katrina, communities learned they couldn't wait for official help. Hong Kong protesters used mesh networks when the government tried to cut them off. Iranian women shared videos of police brutality when the state blocked social media. Puerto Ricans coordinated mutual aid through amateur radio when Maria destroyed the grid.
The pattern is clear: when systems fail - whether from natural disasters or deliberate suppression - communities need tools to build their own infrastructure. Communities united in purpose and vision can be powerful.
When you contribute to Abhaya, you're investing in infrastructure that makes communities fearless. No CEO can sell it. No government can buy it. No algorithm can suppress it. No storm can wash it away.
Every dollar helps us turn individual devices into collective power. Like Powell said - we're not waiting for someone to save us. We're using what's already in our hands to build the infrastructure of fearlessness.
Fund the network that makes communities fearless.
We're assembling an international team of developers and engineers who understand that code is power, and power should belong to the people. If you're a technologist looking to put your skills toward meaningful resistance, this is how you push back against authoritarianism and corporate overreach.
• Onion Router, I2P, Freenet protocols
• DevOps/SecOps fluent in Dark Web technologies
This is open-source work with no revenue model - Abhaya is designed to be free for all communities. For technologists feeling the weight of current events, it's a concrete way to turn skills into direct action and fulfill civic duty through code. Ready to put your shoulder to the wheel of progress? Reach out.
Because true community care means building the infrastructure that makes us all fearless.

content:
Fundraiser by Hong Kong Forum : 自由雕塑公園之『香港地』香港抗爭者雕像金屬牌匾 及 新壁畫
Hong Kong Forum for Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles
Hong Kong Forum for Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles
Hong Kong Forum is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles.
Hong Kong Forum for Hong Kong Forum Los Angeles
5年過去了，彷彿一切烽煙已經在時間中沈沒，然而有些人仍然選擇不去遺忘。
Five years have passed since Hong Konger's last attempt to maintain their freedom, and it seems that all dust has settled. However, some people still choose not to forget.
經過多方努力，我們在Yermo的自由雕塑公園（Liberty Sculpture Park）建立起了香港地，用藝術去銘記香港人的意志不滅。
After many efforts, we have established Hong Kong Corner in the Liberty Sculpture Park in Yermo, using art to remember the unyielding will of the Hong Kongers.
香港地的維護和創作需要長期的投入，我們亟需你的支持。不論捐款多少，都代表著你對香港所出的一分力。
The maintenance and creation of Yermo's "Hong Kong Corner" requires long-term investment, and we urgently need your support. Any donation, no matter the amount, represents your contribution to the undying spirit of Hong Kongers.
We hope to meet in a free Hong Kong someday.
Donation serves 3 main purposes.
1. 現時香港地有四件展品，沙漠氣候極端，冬寒夏焰，烈日風沙，我們要定期維修，提供防曬材料予連儂牆， 令他們可以日久維新。
1. Currently, Hong Kong Corner has four exhibits. We need to perform regular maintenance for some of the art works and provide sun & water protection sealants in the harsh desert weather condition.
2. 香港抗爭者的雕像現時沒有任何解釋。 在我們維修的過程當中，經常見到美國本地人到訪，但他們對於2019抗爭一事並不了清楚。希望可以籌款建立一塊金屬牌匾， 刻上中英文描述，令到到訪者了解究竟發生了什麼事。
2. The statues of Hong Kong Protesters currently have no explanations. During our maintenance work, we often see local Americans visiting, but they are not familiar with the 2019 protests. We hope to raise funds to establish a metal plaque with descriptions in both Chinese and English to help visitors understand what happened.
3. 自由雕塑公園的創辦人陳維明老師亦為香港地建立了新牆，我們希望可以籌款聘請來自香港的專業藝術家，以壁畫描繪出香港的景況。
3. Mr. Chen Wei Ming, the art creator of Liberty Sculpture Park, has also built a new wall for Hong Kong Land. We hope to raise funds to pay for the expenses of hiring a professional artist from Hong Kong to depict the situation in Hong Kong with a mural.

content:
Fundraiser by Su Lee : Wipe Away Su Lee's Tears from her Composing Nights
Su Lee is organizing this fundraiser.
Dear friends, music lovers, and new music supporters,
It’s me, Su Lee, and I am currently working on my dissertation concert (for my Ph.D. in composition) which will be held on Sept. 9th 2019 Monday at 7:30pm in Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall at University at Buffalo.
The title of my dissertation composition and concert is Die Radikalen Tasten (The Radical Keys) in terms of aesthetics, Klang (sound), and theme.
I am writing a concerto for organ with keyboard ensemble, namely for our own tremendous Fisk Op.95 organ at UB. It will involve organ soloist with 1 assistant, 2 pianos (1 quarter-tone flat piano), 2 harpsichords (1 quarter-tone flat harpsichord), and 2 vibraphones which is a very rare instrumentation for microtonal new music.
The 1st half of the program features significant keyboard works from the 20th century such as Messiaen's solo organ work and Ives's quarter-tone piano pieces. As a special request from Dr. Fuller, who was in charge of the installation of the Fisk Op.95 organ at UB, I'm playing my very first organ transcription of Wagner's orchestral work.
The 2nd half of the program features my own 'radical' politically inspired compositions including a choral piece with organ accompaniment (dedicated to the UUCB Choir family) and my dissertation organ concerto. Both works are based on the Korean Democratic Uprising in May 1980 and the protest song written for the victims of the subsequent Gwangju massacre - a song that has became widely popular for activists and protesters, including those participating in the on-going Hong Kong protests.
Overall, it is a very colorful and unique combination and a rare program which is a you-don’t-want-to-miss concert.
I am modestly asking you for a little or big help in making my dissertation concert happen smoothly, especially given my financial struggles in not being able to even work legally for money off campus in America due to my visa status.
Your generous donation will be spent towards, (besides helping me wipe away all my tears and whining from composing numerous nights over the past few months and rehearsing in the upcoming days and nights):
Nine Musicians’ Performance Fee, about $3,000 – 3,300
Rent/Labor for Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall, about $1,000
Other concert related costs; buying performing materials, copying/binding score/parts, printing poster/program book, audio/video recording, photographing, tuning, reception, etc. about $1,200 – 1,500
Fortunately, I got awarded the MDRF (research fund) for $3,000 at UB so that I can be reimbursed afterwards, but I need money upfront now to pay first, and possibly more, to pay my dream team musicians fairly and to cover other costs.
Your genuine help means SO MUCH to me being an international Ph.D. student with many restrictions on earning money (3 months summer break without job, seriously!), as it will lighten my financial burdens and psychological anxiety when I absolutely need to focus more on my creative activities.
Simply speaking, you are contributing to a potentially "fabulous" new music piece, stimulating my further musical activities and making me believe that life (and the world) is so beautiful!
Every single one of your names will be acknowledged in my concert program book, and to thank you all, but not nearly enough, I like to give you in return as below:
$1~$49: a thank-you-card with a cover of a handwritten excerpt of my score
$50~$99: a thank-you-card like above AND a dvd of my dissertation concert (after my concert)
$100~$199: a thank-you-card AND a dvd like above, PLUS the autographed full score of my dissertation composition
$200~$299: EVERYTHING above AND one additional dvd of my Masters organ recitals (your choice of “Über den Namen B-A-C-H” or “Celebrating Lou Harrison’s 100th Birth-Year at Thunder Night”)
$300 or more: EVERYTHING above, PLUS a gift pack of Korean snacks/sweets/tea etc.
Please write me an email with your home address!
I am really excited to prepare my dissertation concert. Though I feel like this is sadly going to be my last self designed concert during my time in Buffalo (at UB), so I cannot wait to see many of you there!
Thank you so much for reading this and considering your donation.
I promise to pay you back with my "fabulous" new compositions and my performance, with the great help of my dream team of musician fellows!
Please feel free to spread the link to your social pages like Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter, or to emails, to help get the word out!
FYI, I am collecting your donations from now till October and GoFundMe takes 2.9% for transaction fee plus $0.30 PER Donation. Or you can donate by sending me a check to my place (email me for asking my address please!)

summary: Fundraiser by Hillary Johnson : Hong Kong Photojournalism Trip Hillary Johnson is organizing this fundraiser. Hi everyone, my name is Hillary Johnson, and I’m a photographer living in Chicago, working all over the Midwest and in Hong Kong.
content:
Fundraiser by Hillary Johnson : Hong Kong Photojournalism Trip
Hillary Johnson is organizing this fundraiser.
Hi everyone, my name is Hillary Johnson, and I’m a photographer living in Chicago, working all over the Midwest and in Hong Kong. I have two main threads to my photography practice, photojournalism and fine art.
Though it feels awkward, I confess, I’m pushing ahead because I need your help.
I’m going to Hong Kong on November 12 to cover the protest and the election of a new cabinet in Hong Kong.
You might wonder why bother giving money to me or why my voice particular needs to be added to this news event, or even why this matters to you at all. I hear that and I’ll do my best to answer your questions. I’ll also explain what you can do if you’re interested in helping out.
A little bit about me: in addition to being a photographer I’m also someone who studies a martial art called Ving Tsun. This art is extremely popular in Hong Kong for various reasons that I won’t go into right now but if you’re curious you can ask me and I’ll be happy to answer. It was the practice of this martial art that introduced me to my husband, Matt Johnson who runs a kung fu school here in Chicago.
This martial art has a code of ethics that involves being a good citizen, being humble, promoting peace, and standing up for what is right and protecting those who need protection from bullies and so forth.
I made my first trip to Hong Kong a couple of years ago and I’ve been back a few times since then. Though I’m someone who likes spend a lot of time in remote locations being quiet and letting the busyness of my mind and heart settle down, I felt 100% in love with the city of Hong Kong, it’s culture, it’s people, and of course with my kung fu family there.
As a result it has been difficult watching the news and worrying about this place I love so much and the people who live there.
My concern for all of this led me to do a story for the Chicago Reader.
Here's a link to that: https://www.chicagoreader.com/chicago/photos-hong-kong-protest-freedom/Content?oid=73815391
I’m extremely grateful to the reader for giving me the time and space that it did. I made all the photographs, did all the interviews, and wrote all the text with guidance from the amazing Reader staff. In the process of working on that story I began to see, that much that was going on in Hong Kong seems to not quite be making it into the news. This made me want to go to Hong Kong and do more.
The stories we have been seeing her only the tip of the iceberg. I’m interested in the stories of ordinary people, their everyday life, and what they do.
How do they support each other in the midst of such extreme difficulty?
I want to understand the impact of what’s happening in this interaction between the Beijing mainland Chinese government in the city of Hong Kong in the Hong Kong people.
It’s interesting that Hong Kong has roots and connections stretching out from the city, all over the globe. While working on the story I’ve met many people here in Chicago who have a deep connections to Hong Kong.
I want to go and photograph an interview to help amplify the voices of those people not being heard as much as they might be.
Why do the events Hong Kong matter to you wherever you might live?
Number one. Hong Kong people are simply asking for fundamental human rights to be recognized.
Number two. The Hong Kong people are asking for the promises made by the Chinese government to be kept.
Number three. The Hong Kong people want their freedom.
All people everywhere around the world want their fundamental human rights, they want promises to be kept and they want freedom.
If we all look into our own hearts I believe we will see this truth is self evident.
What’s happening in Hong Kong matters to all of us, because all of us want the same things; freedom, respect- both given and received, dignity, and agency.
Further, for those of us living in other parts of the world, if we think that what’s happening in Hong Kong cannot happen to us wherever it is that we happen to live, I think if you forgive me, that view is naïve.
The road to tyranny is a slippery slope.
First one right is eroded, then another, then another.
For this trip to Hong Kong all the groundwork is in place.
Because of the network being built up over the years and as a result of my recent work, there are people on the ground in Hong Kong ready to help with making connections, translation, safety and getting around and so forth.
My intention is to get to Hong Kong do my work at the photographer and then do my best to get those stories out into the world so that everyone can know what is going on.
But I need help with the expenses.
Airfare and hotel around $2100-2400 depending on flight details
Transportation in Hong Kong When the MTR is shut down taxis may be necessary - estimating maybe $300
Money to pay translators and other fixtures and facilitators estimating $300-500
A laptop to process photos while I’m there so I can send them out to editors at various news outlets - around $200-300
I’m hoping to raise $3500. to cover all of that as well as some of my bills while I’m away so that the lights and heat are still on when I return home.
Addition I’ll provide links to news outlets as well as the story I did for the reader so that you can get more information about the situation over there.
I’ll also link or attach a video that I made about the story.
As things when I’m planning to offer in addition to publicly thinking everyone who supports this is the creation of a private Facebook group where I post updates photos and video from my time in Hong Kong.
This content will be exclusively for anyone who supports this trip.
I’m excited to announce that someone already made a first donation of $500 before even launched this campaign which let me adjust the amount needed to $3500
Honestly I wasn’t even planning on doing this but so many people said to me that they wanted to support the trip and believe in the mission of supporting truth and openness and democracy, that I pushed past my own discomfort and jumped in.
I want to thank all of you in advance for your support and help.
Please know that even if you can’t donate money to this trip, I’d be very grateful for your repeated sharing of the campaign. We all know how this works, and whether we like it or not it requires a certain diligence. A lather rinse and repeat process.
For those of you who can donate, please know how grateful I am for your support. And that no donation is too small or too large.
Again my heartfelt thanks. You should know also that I’ve never felt more sense of mission or purpose in going after story. This has my whole heart and I hope very much but I’ll find out that’s for publishing material of the world to know what is going on in Hong Kong at this critical time in history.
As a final note, I want to add that one of the things I’ve heard lately, is that China may be starting to crack down on the practice of martial arts.
This truly is history repeating itself. This happened during the period of conflict between the Ming and Qing dynasty.
It happened again during the cultural revolution.
And now it’s happening once again.
Why does China always clamp down on martial artists?
Because martial artists, as part of their training, learn how important it is to stand up and fight when it’s necessary. The core of traditional martial arts is about values that respect all people and offer protection to those who need it.
I like to think that with my camera I’m bringing the spirit of kung fu, of the Ving Tsun I love, to my practice using my camera to help protect and defend those in Hong Kong.
I hope that you’ll join me in this fight.
Let me know what questions you may have.
Happy to try my best to answer.
May all be safe, happy, strong and at ease. ❤️

Experience Japan: Arts, Crafts, Culture & Travel Tips! Wed Nov 18 @ 6:30pm, Wed, Nov 18, 2026, 6:30 PM | Meetup
Experience Japan: Arts, Crafts, Culture & Travel Tips! Wed Nov 18 @ 6:30pm
Join the Travel & Culture Group for a special evening celebrating Japan! We're partnering with the Japan Outreach Initiative (JOI) at the University of Nebraska, and the Omaha Sister City direct for Shizuoka, Japan, to bring you an interactive cultural experience filled with Japanese traditions, hands-on activities, and travel inspiration!
Thanks to these wonderful Japanese organizations, rather than simply hearing about Japan, you'll have the opportunity to experience different aspects of Japanese culture firsthand. Throughout the evening, you can explore a variety of cultural activity stations to get hand-on with Japanese culture:
- Kimono & Obi Experience (try on traditional Japanese kimono brought from Japan!)
We'll be welcoming a special guest from the Omaha Sister Cities Association, representing Omaha's sister city of Shizuoka, Japan. They'll give us an in-depth seminar about Japan's incredible destinations, travel tips, where to visit and why, plus the cultural differences that make visiting Japan such a memorable experience.
Whether you've traveled to Japan before, are planning your first trip, or have simply dreamed of visiting, this is a wonderful opportunity to learn more about the country from people with firsthand cultural knowledge.
This event is at the German American Society, which is opening just for our Travel & Culture Group. We’ll have plenty of parking, a variety of drinks for purchase, including imported German beer, spirits, and refreshing non-alcoholic options.

content:
It's not turkey! Lunch at Lalibela, Sun, Nov 29, 2026, 1:00 PM | Meetup
Have you tried Lalibela? Their vegetarian platter is sensational, and oh yes--gigantic. Join us for a fun lunch.
Their vegan, gluten-free vegetarian platter easily feeds two. I order one for myself because I LOVE the leftovers.
Super-duper health benefits in Ethiopian foods:
https://www.yahoo.com/health/u-s-african-diet-swap-has-dramatic-impact-on-117607153277.html
(No need to RSVP if you can't join us.)
Omaha Forks Over Knives is a lively group celebrating the health benefits of a whole-foods, plant-based, no-oil diet. Each of us is in a different place with foods we do and do not consume; we're not The Food Police. We're here to support and learn from each other. (While we're at it, we entertain each other as well.) If you're new to this, we ask that, at a minimum, you confine your food choices in these meetups to plant-based options.
Questions? Watch the documentary Forks Over Knives available to stream on youtube, Netflix, or available on DVD at the Omaha Public Library, then give us a try!

content:
Zion and Bryce Hiking and Glamping, Thu, Nov 12, 2026, 7:00 AM | Meetup
Unreal hoodoos? Check. Slot canyons? Majestic overlooks? Check. All this and more (like heated tents with electricity) await you during our Women’s Hiking and Glamping in Zion National Park and Bryce Canyon weekend adventure!
BRYCE CANYON HIKING AND BEGINNER-FRIENDLY CANYONEERING
Escape to prehistoric Utah where you’ll hike stupid-pretty trails in Zion National Park and Bryce Canyon National Park. Wade through the Virgin River below 1,500′ canyon walls in the Narrows. Spend an entire day exploring Bryce Canyon National Park. Ghost the tourists as you wander deep into orange hoodoos. Explore areas of Zion so remote, they can only be reached by rappelling, scrambling, and down-climbing on a beginner-friendly canyoneering route.
Beastmaster up the West Rim Trail to Scout Lookout and enjoy some of the best views in Zion National Park. You’ll hike through Refrigerator Canyon, and shimmy up all 21 of Walters Wiggles to Scout Lookout with panoramic views of Zion Canyon and Virgin River. Afterward, dry your pits as you descend the trail to an easier hike around the scenic streams of Upper and Lower Emerald Pools.
Every night you’ll rest your head in Insta-worthy glamping tents bordering Zion National Park. Kick it by the campfire under a diamond sky with goddesses who aren’t afraid to get dirty.
See the website for full itinerary, details and to book.

summary: Fundraiser by Mark Nygate : SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE Mark Nygate is organizing this fundraiser. We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help. 我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。 In 2018,
content:
Fundraiser by Mark Nygate : SAVE US FROM THE MEGA EMBASSY! SUPPORT OUR LEGAL CHALLENGE
Mark Nygate is organizing this fundraiser.
We are 100 families taking on the CCP - and we need your help.
我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」，由約一百戶職工家庭組成。我們懇請你伸出援手。
In 2018, our homes-key-worker flats in Tower Hamlets were sold in a secretive deal to the People's Republic of China. We had no say. No warning. And now, we face living under the shadow of a hostile superpower.
2018年，我們居住的Tower Hamlets地段，在未經通知、無任何諮詢下，被秘密售予中國政府。我們無從置喙，如今更面對一個敵對政權的威脅。
The UK Government is expected to approve plans to build the largest embassy in Europe - right here, at Royal Mint Court, next to the Tower of London… and directly on top of our homes.
英國政府即將批准於倫敦塔旁的皇家鑄幣廠（Royal Mint Court）興建歐洲最大規模的中國大使館，預定地點正正位於我們所居之上。
This is not just a planning dispute.
我們擔憂的不僅是一項城市規劃決策，而是一場關乎國家安全、人身安全與基本權利的危機。
China has never shown any regard for our safety - and now the Government and the Metropolitan Police have abandoned us too.
自2018年起，中國政府從未就此提供明確回應，我們甚至不知道會否被驅逐、是否仍能繼續安居於此。而如今，政府與執法機關也對我們置之不理。
We are the Royal Mint Court Residents Association. People backed our previous Crowdfunder campaign that helped pay for a barrister to present our evidence including an independent security assessment showing the serious risks to us from a terror attack on the mega-embassy.
我們是「皇家鑄幣廠居民協會」。我們之前的眾籌活動獲得許多人的支持，資助我們聘請資深大律師提交證據，包括一份獨立的安全評估報告，指出超級大使館可能帶來的恐襲風險。
We are now launching an urgent legal challenge - a Judicial Review - to change the law and stop this injustice.
我們現在正展開一項緊急法律挑戰 — 即司法覆核 — 希望改變現行法律，阻止這場不公。
We need your help to protect our community from the mighty Chinese Communist Party.
我們需要你的幫助，去保護我們的社區，免受強大的中國共產黨威脅。
Whatever you can spare us, will help David stand-up to Goliath.
We are seeking to pursue a Judicial Review because we have believed all along that the planning process has been flawed. Here are some of the reasons we think are likely to be relevant:
我們決定提起司法覆核，是因為我們始終認為整個規劃程序存在問題。以下是我們認為可能相關的一些原因：
“Closed mind”: Ministers may have signalled early approval to China, before formal procedures were followed, breaking the law and abusing planning powers. In a similar vein, objections disappeared after UK ministers returned from Beijing. Residents have felt like pawns in a geopolitical game since the start.
預設立場：部長們可能在正式程序開始前就向中方表示支持，違反法律並濫用規劃權力。在部長們從北京回來之後，原有的反對聲音突然消失。居民們從一開始就覺得自己成了地緣政治博弈中的棋子。
Security concerns: Building a fortified embassy with homes on site and critical infrastructure nearby, ignoring espionage concerns and the real human risk to dissidents, is indefensible.
安全隱患：在住宅區內及重要基礎設施附近建設高度防禦的大使館，無視間諜活動與對異見人士的人身威脅，完全不能接受。
Procedural unfairness: We were shut out of the process. No consultation. No transparency. No respect for the people who live here.
程序不公：我們被完全排除在決策過程之外。無諮詢、無透明、無對居民的尊重。
Legitimate expectation: We were promised due process and protection. We got silence.
合理期望落空：我們被承諾將獲程序保障與保護，實際卻是得不到任何保障。
We still live here. 100 families. Nurses, teachers, pensioners. Our 100 homes are on land now owned by the Chinese government. That means the Chinese ambassador is our landlord - with rights to enter our homes.
我們仍然住在這裡 ，足足一百戶家庭，包括護士、教師、退休人士。我們的一百個住所現已位於中國政府擁有的土地上。這代表中國大使成為我們的業主，有權進入我們的住所。
China refuses to answer us. Since 2018, we’ve begged for assurances: will we be evicted? Will we be safe? Can we stay? Beijing’s answer: not until we get planning permission. This refusal, and the proposal to install a temporary style wooden boundary fence as a dividing line, raises fears that the Chinese Government intends to take back the entire 100 apartments at St Mary Graces Court once they secure diplomatic status for the site, leaving us homeless.
中國拒絕回應我們的訴求。自2018年起，我們不斷尋求保證：我們會被驅逐嗎？我們是否安全？我們能否繼續居住？北京的答覆是：等規劃許可下來再說。這種拒絕，以及擬議中以臨時木欄分隔的做法，讓我們擔心中國政府一旦取得外交地位，將會收回整個St Mary Graces Court的100個單位，使我們流離失所。
This embassy is a fortress. It’s not a normal diplomatic building. It will have secret communications centres, fortified walls, and surveillance technology that can monitor our entire estate, even our bedrooms. It will also stand on top of critical UK cables that MI5 warn are a security risk to the UK.
這座大使館是一個堡壘，並非普通的外交建築。它將設有秘密通訊設施、加固圍牆、監控技術，可監視整個屋苑，甚至包括我們的睡房。而它的地基下方，更有英國重要電纜 ，MI5曾警告這是對國家安全的威脅。
The UK Government knows the risk - and ignored it. Our independent security report warns that this site puts families and national security at risk. Even the UK’s Head of Counter-Terrorism originally objected - citing threats to residents and dissidents. But since ministers returned from Beijing, objections have mysteriously vanished.
英國政府明知有風險，卻選擇無視。我們的獨立安全報告指出，該地點將危害居民與國家安全。甚至連英國反恐部門首長最初也曾反對 ， 指出對居民與異見人士的威脅。但自從部長從北京回來後，這些反對聲音神秘地消失。
Ministers made no mention of the 100 families living here. We are alarmed that the letters from Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and Foreign Secretary David Lammy have ignored the fact that UK families live in 100 apartments on the land that is actually part of Royal Mint court - and is owned by the Chinese government. Our Resident’s Chairman has personally appealed to ministers, submitted the full Crilly Consultants security report, and our plight has appeared in The Times, FT, BBC, CNN, and more. What is happening to democratic accountability in this country?
部長們從未提及這裡有一百戶居民。我們對內政大臣Yvette Cooper及外交大臣David Lammy的信件感到震驚，因為他們完全忽略了皇家鑄幣廠的土地上住有英國公民、100個家庭。我們的居民協會主席曾親自致函部長、提交完整的Crilly安全報告，而我們的處境亦已被《泰晤士報》、《金融時報》、BBC、CNN等多間媒體報導。英國民主問責制度何在？
The first duty of the UK government is to protect its citizens. We understand the UK’s diplomatic obligations - but not at the expense of its own people. The refusal to acknowledge the basic risks of housing a high-security foreign embassy on top of a residential block is deeply troubling. It appears the government is prioritising relations with Beijing over the safety of its own citizens.
英國政府的首要職責是保護其國民。我們明白外交義務，但不能以犧牲本國人民為代價。將一個高安全級別的外國大使館設於住宅區上方，而拒絕承認基本風險，是極度令人不安的。
It’s not just about us. Dissidents, including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese exile communities are terrified. They’ve told us they no longer feel safe protesting outside the site, and on British soil. Their presence, and ours, will be met with constant surveillance and intimidation by a regime known to harass and threaten activists - even abroad.
這件事不僅關係到我們。流亡港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人及中國異見社群皆感到恐懼。他們表示不再敢在該地點或英國土地上公開抗議。他們與我們一樣，將面對來自這個以恐嚇異見者聞名的政權的持續監控與威嚇。
The people have spoken, and they support us.
On 8 February 2025, thousands of British citizens - including Hong Kongers, Uyghurs, Tibetans, Taiwanese and Chinese pro-democracy activists, and human rights campaigners - gathered outside Royal Mint Court in protest against this embassy.
2025年2月8日，數以千計的英國公民 ，包括港人、維吾爾人、西藏人、台灣人、中國民主人士與人權倡議者， 齊集皇家鑄幣廠，抗議中國大使館計劃。
They were joined by cross-party MPs, journalists, and allies. Together, they said NO to the Chinese embassy, and YES to democratic values, safety, and justice.
他們與跨黨派議員、記者及盟友並肩站立，一同說出明確立場：反對中國大使館，支持民主、安全與公義。
Further mass protests followed on 15 March, 3 May, and 14 June - showing growing national resistance to the plan.
3月15日、5月3日及6月14日亦舉行後續大型集會，反對聲浪日益壯大。
They continue to protest, and have made it clear: they won’t stop until this mega-embassy deal is over.
抗議仍在持續，並清楚表示：他們不會停止，直至該項目取消為止。
But the Government is not listening.
But we need your help - fast.
The legal fees for a Judicial Review are beyond the reach of ordinary families. But with your help, we can stand up to both Beijing and Whitehall.
司法覆核的法律費用遠超普通家庭的負擔。但在您的幫助下，我們能夠與北京和英國政府對抗。
This case is about more than one building. It’s about:
Protecting British citizens from state overreach
Defending UK democracy from foreign influence
Challenging backroom deals that put power over people
If we succeed, we won’t just protect our homes. We’ll set a precedent that no foreign government can build on British soil without respecting British citizens and British values.
如若成功，我們不僅能保護我們的家園，我們更是創下先例：任何外國政府不得在罔顧英國公民和英國價值的前提下在英國土地上建造任何建築。
Please chip in whatever you can. £10. £100. £1,000. Every penny goes to legal costs to take this to court. We are a group of teachers, nurses, shop workers and pensioners. We don’t have the Chinese Communist Party’s millions - but with your help, we do have people power.
請您捐出任何您能負擔的金額 — 不論是 £10，£100 還是 £1,000。每一分錢都將用於支付法律費用，讓我們將此案帶上法庭。我們只是一群教師、護士、店員和退休人士。雖然我們沒有中國共產黨的龐大資金 — 但在您的幫助下，我們擁有的是人民的力量。
Because if they can do this to us, they can do it to anyone.
This is a secure UK-based platform, fully registered and subject to UK law.
It is widely used to support political and legal campaigns, including by MPs, NGOs, and grassroots movements - some of which are openly critical of the Chinese government.
該平台廣泛用於支持政治和法律活動，包括國會議員、非政府組織和基層運動 — 包括曾公開批評中國政府的政治活動。
The platform offers full transparency, with public donation records and payment processing via Stripe or PayPal.
該平台提供完全透明的捐款記錄，並通過 Stripe 或 PayPal 處理支付。
There is no history of censorship or compliance with pressure from the Chinese state.
It adheres strictly to GDPR regulations, ensuring donor and campaigner data is protected.
平台嚴格遵守 GDPR 規範，確保捐款者和活動者的數據安全。
2.95% + 0.25 of each donation goes to the platform; 100% of the remaining funds will be used to cover legal costs.
每筆捐款將扣除 2.95% 加 £0.25 之平台手續費，其餘款項將全數用以支付法律相關費用。
If the legal case is dismissed, your donation will be directed to charity unless you request a refund. If you would like your donation returned, please email us. We will calculate and refund your contribution (with platform fee deducted).
如法律訴訟最終被駁回，捐款將撥捐予慈善機構，除非閣下主動申請退款。如欲索回捐款，請電郵至，我們將在扣除平台手續費後，計算並退還閣下之捐款。
We will post updates every two weeks, which you can follow directly on this page.

content:
Fundraiser by Pie Formosa : Support Pie Formosa’s Independent Work
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Inspire others and help Pie build momentum.
Pie Formosa is organizing this fundraiser.
I sometimes describe myself as a refugee from WeChat to Instagram — but I am also, quite literally, a refugee from China.
I am a political dissident, human rights activist, non-binary person and independent writer living with invisible disabilities, now continuing my work in Europe.
I write and create public work about censorship, authoritarianism, political memory, democracy, queer and trans freedom, refugee experiences, neurodiversity, and the cultural spaces where resistance survives.
For years, WeChat was one of the places where I published my work. Readers could easily support independent creators with small tips. Then the Chinese Communist Party shut down my account. I lost not only a platform, but also an audience, an archive, and a simple way for people to support my work.
This fundraiser is part of rebuilding that independence.
Living with invisible disabilities also means that conventional employment structures and constant high-intensity workloads are not always accessible or sustainable for me. I need a modest and stable income to make independent research, writing and human-rights work sustainable.
* research, writing and documentation
* travel to human-rights, democracy and civil-society events
* basic living costs that allow me to continue this work independently
If something I have written, documented or created has informed, helped or inspired you, even €1, €5 or €10 helps me keep this work alive. If donating is not possible, sharing this fundraiser also makes a real difference.
Authoritarianism depends on silence and forgetting. Independent voices survive because people choose to keep them alive.
Thank you for supporting my work.

Alan’s fund provides groceries and rent for a political dissident facing exile abroad
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Inspire others and help Alan build momentum.
Alan Wan is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Alan, and I am writing this with a sincere and humble heart.
I am a Chinese political dissident living in Houston, Texas. Because of my beliefs and my willingness to speak openly about freedom, human rights, and justice, I have faced serious threats and intimidation from the Chinese government. These pressures have made it impossible for me to safely return to China, where my family still lives. Every day, I carry the pain of being separated from my loved ones, uncertain when—or if—I will ever be able to reunite with them again.
Beyond the emotional suffering, I am now facing severe financial hardship. Due to restrictions and complications surrounding the transfer of my personal funds from abroad, I have been unable to access resources that I once depended on for survival. My savings are rapidly disappearing, and I am now struggling simply to cover basic daily necessities such as food, housing, transportation, and medical care.
This situation has left me feeling isolated and vulnerable. I never imagined that standing by my principles would lead to such profound personal sacrifice, but I continue to hold onto hope.
Today, I am reaching out with deep humility to ask for your support. Any assistance—whether financial help, practical resources, or connections to organizations that aid individuals in political exile—would mean more than words can express. Your kindness could help me maintain stability during this incredibly difficult chapter of my life and allow me to continue moving forward with dignity.
I am not asking for luxury, only for the chance to live safely and meet my most basic needs while I navigate these extraordinary challenges.
Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Your compassion, understanding, and support would be a lifeline during one of the hardest periods of my life.

Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

华盛顿，11 月 4 日。/塔斯社/。德克萨斯大学国际关系与全球研究项目前主任、匹兹堡大学（宾夕法尼亚州）名誉教授、美国国务院和五角大楼前顾问迈克尔·布伦纳对塔斯社表示，美国国会中期选举的结果不会对华盛顿的外交政策产生重大影响，因为几乎整个美国政治阶层都在寻求孤立俄罗斯、遏制中国和北约扩张。
这位政治分析人士认为，“通过预算拨款和高级任命人员的确认，[美国]国会组成的变化只能产生边际效应。”
布伦纳表示，无论中期选举结果如何，两党在重大外交政策问题上都将保持更广泛的共识。布伦纳表示：“这包括维护美国的全球主导地位；削弱/遏制中国不断增长的实力；孤立俄罗斯并扩大北约；胁迫委内瑞拉等弱国获得经济和安全优势。” “随之而来的行动几乎得到了该国政治阶层的普遍支持，”他补充道。
“在乌克兰问题上，没有变化，”分析师预测。他表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将继续推动“短期协议和长期和解”。与此同时，华盛顿建制派的大部分人已经将俄罗斯视为战略敌人，其中“民主党人是最热情的”，他总结道。
周二，36 个州的州长选举也同时举行，参议院 100 个席位中只有 35 个席位以及众议院全部 435 个席位进行了角逐。执政的共和党目前控制着参众两院。下届第 120 届国会将根据中期选举结果召开，将于 2027 年 1 月 3 日开始召开。

Virtually all US elites seek to isolate Russia, contain China, expand NATO — expert
Changes in the composition of the [US] Congress could have only a marginal effect via budget appropriations and confirmation of senior appointees, the political analyst argued
WASHINGTON, November 4. /TASS/. The results of the midterm Congressional election in the United States will not have a major effect on Washington’s foreign policy as virtually the entire US political class is seeking Russia’s isolation, containment of China and NATO’s expansion, Michael Brenner, former Director of the International Relations & Global Studies Program at the University of Texas, honorary professor at the University of Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania), and former Consultant to the US Department of State and the Pentagon, told TASS.
"Changes in the composition of the [US] Congress could have only a marginal effect via budget appropriations and confirmation of senior appointees," the political analyst argued.
According to Brenner, regardless of the results of the midterms, a broader bipartisan consensus on major foreign policy issues will be maintained. "That includes preserving the US. dominant global position; undermining/containing China’s growing strength; isolating Russia and expanding NATO; coercing weak states to obtain economic and security advantages, e.g. Venezuela," Brenner opined. "Attendant actions have had almost universal backing from the country’s political class," he added.
"On Ukraine, no change," the analyst predicted. US President Donald Trump will continue to promote "a short-term deal and longer-term conciliation," he opined. Meanwhile, the larger part of the Washington Establishment has already designated Russia as a strategic enemy, with "Democrats being the most passionate," he concluded.
Only 35 out of 100 Senate seats and all 435 seats in the House were contested on Tuesday when a gubernatorial election across 36 states was also held. The ruling Republican party currently holds control of both houses. The next, 120th Congress, that will be crafted by the results of the midterms, will begin sitting on January 3, 2027.

title: 人物專訪之四 許淑華：中共正在洗年輕人認知
summary: 北市松山信義議員許淑華接受《大紀元時報》專訪。（大紀元） 【大紀元2026年11月04日訊】（大紀元記者常懷仁台灣台北報導）爭取連任的台北市松山信義議員許淑華接受本報專訪時表示，中共現在會招待台灣35歲以下的年輕人過去中國認知他們、使用抖音或小紅書等軟體，甚至工作，目的就是讓年輕人對中國有好感，而她也認為雙城論壇成為政治場域，台北市應舉辦國際論壇，也提到高雄的演唱會經濟帶來的好處，並提出台北可以讓企業認養古蹟的方式。 許淑華接受《大紀元時報》專訪時透露，中共現在開始會針對35
content:
北市松山信義議員許淑華接受《大紀元時報》專訪。（大紀元）
【大紀元2026年11月04日訊】（大紀元記者常懷仁台灣台北報導）爭取連任的台北市松山信義議員許淑華接受本報專訪時表示，中共現在會招待台灣35歲以下的年輕人過去中國認知他們、使用抖音或小紅書等軟體，甚至工作，目的就是讓年輕人對中國有好感，而她也認為雙城論壇成為政治場域，台北市應舉辦國際論壇，也提到高雄的演唱會經濟帶來的好處，並提出台北可以讓企業認養古蹟的方式。
許淑華接受《大紀元時報》專訪時透露，中共現在開始會針對35歲以下的年輕人，中共會跟年輕人說，你找同學來就落地招待，只要付機票費用即可或不用付機票費，用青年交流、青年創業平台等方式交流，然後中共會先讓人認識中國，接著帶你看抖音、小紅書等公司，教人怎麼使用。
許淑華繼續描述，若這些年輕人去中國做生意的話，中共可能會幫你付一年的房租，然後媒合你跟中國的青創夥伴一起做地方創生等工作，「目前正在進行」。
許淑華解釋，因為中共認為台灣天然獨的太多了，中共認為現在的年輕人眼睛一打開就是在台灣這塊土地上長大，認知的是中華民國，不知道中國是什麼，這樣下去年輕人會都很討厭中國，所以要讓台灣年輕人知道中國多好，然後洗年輕人對中國的觀感，告訴年輕人，台灣和中國是同文同種，這是她目前擔憂的，政府應該處理。
談到這幾年有不少國際團體前往高雄舉辦演唱會。許淑華坦言，台北的國際能見度很差，這也是她覺得雙城論壇變成政治場域、統戰策略，因為每次簽了MOU，但履約的有多少？少之又少，為何台北要用雙城論壇，而非國際論壇？台北可以跟立陶宛、葡萄牙等國的城市舉辦論壇，若覺得不錯可以簽姐妹市，國際化才是台北市最重要的。
所以，許淑華認為，台北應該把雙城論壇改成國際論壇，呼應沈伯洋的無限城論壇，因欸城市對城市的話，中共也無法阻擾你，如此才能提升台北的國際能見度並行銷台北市，台北除了101、大巨蛋外，還有很多文化資產，如：三井倉庫等。
許淑華接著分析高雄的行銷方式，高雄歡迎所有歌手、國際團體錢去表演，因為不收租金，但是會針對門票收入進行抽成，高雄不收租金的理由是因為這些團體在高雄辦演唱會就會帶動人潮、商業發展、觀光產值，這對政府來說很重要，所以寧願不收門票，但是這是利民政策，因為旅行社、小吃店等都受惠。
許淑華表示，大家都想去高雄的原因是因為實賺，若他是國際知名團體的話，台北的場地費要兩、三百萬，就已經納入成本了，高雄不用場地費，當然去高雄，而且既然是國際團體的話就會自帶流量，辦在哪裡都沒差。
所以，她直言，台北市不能用功利的態度看待，大巨蛋收這麼高的租金，但拿到什麼？台北市只有0.6%的分潤，大巨蛋門票113年收入約4.8億，換算下來只有398萬，這沒有必要。
許淑華提到企業認養古蹟的方式，她說，東京車站當時是三菱地所認養，因為旁邊要做都更，政府就說可以都更，但是要認養車站，因此企業就認養了車站，而且用得很漂亮，還可以行銷，但政府不用出一毛錢。所以，政府也可以讓企業認養松菸。
最後，許淑華總結，高雄為何能增加經濟產值是因為捨棄政府收入，但是要創造利民政策，讓人潮去高雄，這是最重要的，因為說實在的政府收場地租金，也是到大水庫，等同政府首入，沒什麼意義，與其如此，不如讓所有產業活絡起來，這也是很多團體願意去高雄，這是三贏政策。◇

或聯絡Telegram: @ChinaWorkers

在中共的压迫与歧视之下LGBTQ+的困境

2013年，中共官媒曾呼吁公众友善对待同性恋者、消除歧视。然而，近年中国性少数的生存空间不断收窄。LGBTQ支援中心、活动、书店、社群媒体帐号及交友应用程式，已接连遭到关闭。中共对LGBTQ权利倡议活动的「零容忍」态度，正日益扩及海外。2026年，甚至有参加泰国骄傲游行的中国性少数者回国后遭警方盘问。中共的镇压不仅针对性少数，也反映了其对一切独立社会组织的恐惧和敌视。

毛泽东时代，同性恋者被视为「流氓」，文革期间更有人遭到批斗、羞辱和暴力迫害。1970年代后，同性恋者仍可能因「流氓罪」被捕。直到1997年流氓罪废除，同性恋行为才除罪化；2001年，同性恋才被移出中国精神疾病分类。此后，中国逐渐出现同志酒吧、网络社群和民间平权组织。然而，中共始终只容忍有限活动，并对任何可能对其控制权构成哪怕是微小挑战的事物都深感恐惧。

content:
王毅会见沙特安全顾问呼吁对话解决海湾争端|中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 3 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
王毅会见沙特安全顾问呼吁对话解决海湾争端
中国最高外交官王毅在北京会见沙特国家安全顾问艾班，敦促通过对话谈判解决争端，维护中东海湾地区能源和航运安全。
11月3日，中国最高外交官王毅在北京会见沙特国务大臣、内阁成员兼国家安全顾问艾班，就中东海湾地区局势交换意见。
中共中央政治局委员、中央外事办公室主任王毅表示，当前地区局势再次到了战争与和平的关键时刻。他说，尽管通往和平的道路并不平坦，但只要坚持下去，就会取得进展。希望各方通过对话谈判解决争端、结束敌对行动，维护地区能源和航运安全。
王毅表示，中方认为，地区国家应增进相互了解，重建信任，改善关系，和睦相处。他呼吁协商构建符合地区人民长远利益的地区安全新架构。
王毅还表示，中方愿恪守习近平主席就维护地区和平稳定提出的一系列倡议和主张。中方愿与沙特等各方沟通协调，为帮助地区走出当前阴霾、实现持久和平与安全发挥建设性作用。

Wang Yi meets Saudi security adviser, calls for dialogue to resolve Gulf disputes | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 3 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Wang Yi meets Saudi security adviser, calls for dialogue to resolve Gulf disputes
Wang Yi, China's top diplomat, met Saudi National Security Adviser Musaad al-Aiban in Beijing, urging dialogue and negotiation to resolve disputes and safeguard energy and shipping security in the Middle East Gulf region.
China's top diplomat Wang Yi met Saudi Arabia's Minister of State, Cabinet member and National Security Adviser Musaad al-Aiban in Beijing on 3 November, exchanging views on the situation in the Middle East Gulf region.
Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the Central Foreign Affairs Office, said the current regional situation had again reached a critical juncture between war and peace. While the path to peace is not smooth, he said, progress will be made if pursued. He expressed hope that all parties could resolve disputes and end hostilities through dialogue and negotiation, thus safeguarding regional energy and shipping security.
China believes, Wang Yi added, that countries in the region should enhance mutual understanding, rebuild trust, improve relations and live together in harmony. He called for consultations to build a new regional security architecture that serves the long-term interests of the region's people.
Wang Yi also said China is willing to uphold a series of initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on maintaining regional peace and stability. He said Beijing would communicate and coordinate with Saudi Arabia and other parties to play a constructive role in helping the region emerge from the current gloom and achieve lasting peace and security.

资料照片：美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥在纽约联合国大会期间会见日本外相茂木敏充(Motegi Toshimitsu)(右)和韩国外交部长赵显(Cho Hyun)(左)，三国外长在会后发表联合声明。(2026年9月21日)
美国、日本与韩国外长上星期五(10月30日)在亚特兰大举行的20国集团(G20)外长会议期间举行三方会谈。美国国务院说，三方外长在会中再次强调了维持台海和平稳定的重要性；美国国务卿马科尔·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)也在会中提到，中国在南中国海、东中国海及黄海的胁迫行为，以及与俄罗斯的合作都是在破坏印太地区的和平稳定。
旨在为下个月在美国佛罗里达州迈阿密举行的20国集团领导人峰会铺垫的外长会议，讨论议程包括航行自由、能源、粮食及供应链安全的议题。
美国国务院在当天发布的声明中说，卢比奥与日本外相茂木敏充(Motegi Toshimitsu)及韩国外长赵显(Cho Hyun)在会议间隙进行了三方会谈，“审视了促进自由开放印太地区安全与繁荣的三边伙伴关系”，并签署了一个“三边北极太平洋伙伴关系(TAPP)”合作备忘录，以探索在太平洋北极地区的海洋合作与经济伙伴关系。
声明指出，国务卿与两位外长重申他们致力于实现朝鲜民主主义人民共和国的完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会各项决议，包括禁止为朝鲜核计划及弹道导弹项目提供创收支持。
“他们也强调了维护台海和平稳定的重要性。卢比奥国务卿也提出了中国寻求在南中国海确立控制权的举措、其在东中国海及黄海的胁迫行为，以及俄罗斯与中国损害印太地区和平稳定的合作，”声明说。
三国外长前一次会谈是在9月21日联合国大会期间，当时三方会谈后也曾发布联合声明，强调维系台海和平稳定的重要性。
国务院说，此次三人再度确认了该次会面时发布的共同声明，并承诺将继续在所有级别开展三方会谈。
台湾外交部上星期六发布声明表示，外长林佳龙对三国外长再次确认台海和平稳定重要性表达感谢，并欢迎伙伴国家持续透过具体行动维护区域整体和平稳定。
“美日韩三国外长今年已多次公开重申维护台海和平稳定的重要性，充分彰显台海安全攸关区域稳定，已是国际社会高度关切的共同议题，更是维系印太区域和平与繁荣不可或缺的一环，”声明说。
台湾外交部强调，面对中国持续升高对台军事威胁及灰色地带侵扰，台湾将持续与美国及其他理念相近国家深化合作，共同维护台海及印太地区的和平、稳定与繁荣。

# Will New Laws Finally End Human Rights Abuses in Asia’s Factories?

It’s clear that voluntary measures aren’t enough for ethical sourcing and supply chains.

By **Nithin Coca**

November 03, 2026

[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F11%2Fwill-new-laws-finally-end-human-rights-abuses-in-asias-factories%2F&title=Will+New+Laws+Finally+End+Human+Rights+Abuses+in+Asia%E2%80%99s+Factories%3F "Share on LinkedIn")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F11%2Fwill-new-laws-finally-end-human-rights-abuses-in-asias-factories%2F "Share on Facebook")[](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Will+New+Laws+Finally+End+Human+Rights+Abuses+in+Asia%E2%80%99s+Factories%3F%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F11%2Fwill-new-laws-finally-end-human-rights-abuses-in-asias-factories%2F "Share on Bluesky")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Will+New+Laws+Finally+End+Human+Rights+Abuses+in+Asia%E2%80%99s+Factories%3F&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F11%2Fwill-new-laws-finally-end-human-rights-abuses-in-asias-factories%2F "Share on X")

Credit: [Depositphotos](https://depositphotos.com/editorial/chinese-factory-37556413.html)

In 2000, the United Nations Global Compact was founded, and in 2007, it became the main force behind the Geneva Declaration on corporate responsibility. The idea was that companies would, voluntarily and collaboratively, work together to respect human, labor, and environmental rights in their businesses, including along complex supply chains.

The Global Compact was one of many similar initiatives, often spurred by campaigns or investigative journalism reports, that sought to end abuses in supply chains and improve sustainability. The World Benchmarking Alliance setup a corporate [human rights benchmark](https://www.worldbenchmarkingalliance.org/corporate-human-rights-benchmark/), while the Consumer Goods Forum (CGF) launched a [Human Rights Coalition](http://www.theconsumergoodsforum.com/news_updates/human-rights-coalition-welcomes-three-new-members-ahold-delhaize-haleon-and-the-lindt-sprungli-group/). Companies including Cargill, Google, Airbus, and Coca Cola released human rights guidelines that, on paper, looked quite strict, stating clearly. For example, Microsoft [declared that](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/corporate-responsibility/human-rights-statement#tab-key-areas-of-impact) “suppliers must comply fully with all employment laws, share its commitment to respect all human rights… and take effective measures to remedy any adverse human rights impacts.”

Yet, more than 20 years later, the impact of these efforts are less than clear. While some companies have made progress, and shown commitment to better sourcing and monitoring of human rights along their supply chains, many have not.

“With voluntary guidelines, the key issue is the gap between commitment and real life implementation,” said Johannes Blankenbach, a researcher with the non-profit Business and Human Rights Resource Center (BHRRC), to The Diplomat.

The BHRRC and other watchdogs like Human Rights Watch, [Somo](https://www.somo.nl/failures-in-due-diligence-and-workers-rights-protection/), [The Breakthrough Institute](https://thebreakthrough.org/issues/energy/sins-of-a-solar-empire), and [Walk Free](https://www.walkfree.org/news/2025/eu-risking-human-rights-progress-by-weakening-corporate-sustainability-due-diligence-directive/), have found that most companies aren’t meeting their commitments. Across the Global South, especially in Asia, where most goods are manufactured, labor rights continue to be violated by those supplying global brands.

But things are changing. There’s a growing call for mandatory regulations in key importing markets like the United States, Canada, and Europe. This year, new forced labor laws are being passed in places like Vietnam and India, partly due to tariff threats from the United States. While still not universal, they are signs we may be heading to a new paradigm where supply chains are monitored not by nonprofits and the media, but but strict laws and real financial repercussions.

While this will most directly impact countries like China, where state-mandated forced labor of Uyghurs has been well-documented, the entire Asia-Pacific region needs to pay attention or face similar restrictions on foreign market access.

**Why Voluntary Commitments Often Fail**

There are numerous reasons why voluntary efforts have mostly failed to have the impact that was once hoped for. To Blankenbach, a key issue is accountability.

“In the voluntary system, there is no central or reliable oversight. Some was done by NGOs, but due to limited resources, that was not comprehensive, and there was no way to sanction companies that weren’t complying,” said Blankenbach.

In general, organizations like CGF or the U.N. rarely monitored members of their voluntary groupings. It was often non-profits like the BHRRC, or [the media](https://thediplomat.com/2022/04/after-pressure-growing-transparency-in-malaysias-glove-industry/), that exposed the failures of companies to meet their commitments. And even then, the punishment was often little more than public shaming.

“For things like the Global Compact, strongest enforcement would be, maybe, an exclusion of a member,” said Blankenbach.

Another issue is that competitors aren’t always held to the same standards, especially if they’re based outside the United States, Europe, or a few other markets where consumers demand sustainability, like Japan. An American shoe company could invest heavily into making its supply chains ethical, only to see a Chinese or Vietnamese competitor undercut it on costs, and face far less pressure.

路透社報導，美國司法部提出緊急聲請，尋求在逐一查證選民的公民身分前暫停計算這些有爭議的選票，這場法律戰可能影響數以千計選民。
川普所屬的共和黨正力拚在11月3日期中選舉中保住國會控制權。加州是美國人口最多的州，也是民主黨票倉。川普政府在期中選舉前加強關注所謂非公民投票問題。
司法部在向最高法院提出的聲請文件中表示：「一旦加州將遭質疑的選票與合法選票混在一起，就無法再將遭質疑的選票區分出來。」
川普政府請求最高法院下令加州將名單上人員所投的選票與其他選票分開，在確認這些選民具有美國公民身分前不得計票。司法部今天敦促最高法院迅速採取行動，在大法官正式裁定司法部的聲請前先下令暫時擱置這些選票。（編譯：盧映孜）1151103

（中央社西棕櫚灘2日綜合外電報導）一架商務噴射機昨天墜毀在美國佛羅里達州棕櫚灘郡，機上9人全數喪命，當局調查人員今天表示，空難發生之前，飛機部分零件似乎已經脫落。
失事的是一架里爾60型噴射機（Learjet 60），從美國德州奧斯汀（Austin）起飛，原定飛往島國巴哈馬，卻墜毀於佛州棕櫚灘郡（Palm Beach County）一處住宅區附近。
美聯社報導，美國國家運輸安全委員會（National Transportation Safety Board）委員柴普曼（Tom Chapman）於記者會說道，這架噴射機似乎在撞擊地面之前就已開始解體。
柴普曼指出：「我們確實掌握一些跡象，顯示飛機在撞擊之前就開始解體。」
他還提及：「我們可能會在實際撞擊地點相隔一段距離的地方，找到飛機部分零件。」
相關當局尚未公布罹難者姓名，棕櫚灘郡警方拒絕談論這起空難事故的調查，但透露調查仍處於初步階段。
航班追蹤網站Flightradar24數據顯示，失事噴射機的垂直下降速度一度超過每分鐘3萬2000英尺。（編譯：陳彥鈞）1151103

summary: 孟加拉国服装厂因工资抗议升级而再次关闭海峡时报 孟加拉国服装厂因工资抗议演变成暴力活动而再次关闭 现在注册：了解亚洲快速发展的情况 在孟加拉国达卡，服装工人封锁道路，要求提高最低工资，警察发射催泪瓦斯弹。发表于 2026 年 11 月 3 日，上午 01:05 更新于 2026 年 11 月 3 日，上午 01:16 达卡 - 孟加拉国服装厂在前一天大面积停工后于 11 月 2 日短暂恢复运营，但工人和警察之间的新冲突迫使数百家工厂被迫停工。
content:
孟加拉国服装厂因工资抗议升级而再次关闭海峡时报
孟加拉国服装厂因工资抗议升级而再次关闭
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
孟加拉国达卡，服装工人封锁道路，要求提高最低工资，警察发射催泪弹。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 3 日 01:05
更新于 2026 年 11 月 3 日 01:16
达卡 - 孟加拉国的服装工厂在前一天大范围停工后于 11 月 2 日短暂恢复运营，但工人和警察之间的新冲突迫使数百家工厂再次暂停生产。
骚乱引发了人们对孟加拉国发货延误和买家信心的担忧。孟加拉国是 H&M、Zara、沃尔玛和 Primark 等品牌的主要供应商，目前正处于春季和夏季出口订单生产周期的关键时刻。
工人要求将最低月工资从 12,500 塔卡提高到 30,000 塔卡（合 308 新元），他们在主要制造区封锁道路、破坏工厂并与警察发生冲突，导致 679 家工厂停产。
孟加拉国是仅次于中国的全球第二大服装出口国，成衣行业占该南亚国家出口收入的80%以上。它雇用了约 400 万工人，约占经济产出的 10%。
为了化解危机，政府于 11 月 1 日成立了一个由六名成员组成的工资委员会，以审查工人的要求，这些要求在持续的通货膨胀和生活成本上升的情况下得到了加强。
警方表示，在抗议者向警察投掷砖块和石块后，他们使用催泪瓦斯驱散了试图封锁达卡道路的制衣工人。据报道，首都郊区的两个制造中心阿苏利亚和加济布尔也发生了骚乱。
警方和行业官员表示，抗议者放火焚烧了一辆警车，并破坏了一些工厂。
11 月 2 日，孟加拉国加济布尔，警察与制衣工人发生冲突，一辆警车受损。
冲突发生在 11 月 1 日抗议和工厂关闭之后，工人们继续要求提高工资并解决就业不满。
“孟加拉国是世界上服装工资最低的国家之一，”孟加拉国服装和产业工人联合会秘书长、工资委员会工人代表巴布尔·阿赫特 (Babul Akhter) 说。
“如果工厂主无法向工人支付适当的工资，他们应该与国际买家谈判更好的价格。他们不能依靠工资过低的工人来开展业务。”
工厂主表示，该行业面临成本上升、中东冲突导致的能源市场不确定性以及主要出口市场需求放缓的问题。
孟加拉国服装制造商和出口商协会主席马哈茂德·哈桑·汗 (Mahmud Hasan Khan) 表示，骚乱期间约有 20 至 25 家工厂遭到破坏，一家皮革制品工厂的办公室也遭到袭击。
他说：“如果这种情况继续下去，工厂一再被迫关闭，我们将别无选择，只能援引‘不工作，不付工资’的规定。”
2026 年 11 月 2 日，达卡举行要求提高最低工资的抗议活动，警方人员拘留了一名制衣工人。
内政部长萨拉胡丁·艾哈迈德警告要采取强有力的行动：“那些以劳工抗议为幌子，损害工人利益并试图破坏国家稳定的人将受到坚决打击。”

Bangladesh garment factories shut again as wage protests turn violent | The Straits Times
Bangladesh garment factories shut again as wage protests turn violent
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Police personnel fire tear gas shells as garment workers block a road demanding higher minimum wages in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Published Nov 03, 2026, 01:05 AM
Updated Nov 03, 2026, 01:16 AM
DHAKA - Bangladesh’s garment factories briefly resumed operations on Nov 2 after a widespread shutdown a day earlier, but fresh clashes between workers and police forced hundreds of plants to suspend production again.
The unrest has raised concerns over shipment delays and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, a key supplier to brands including H&M, Zara, Walmart and Primark, at a critical point in the production cycle for spring and summer export orders.
Workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (S$308), up from 12,500 taka, blocked roads, vandalised factories and clashed with police across major manufacturing districts, prompting 679 factories to halt production.
Bangladesh is the world’s second-largest garment exporter after China and the ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of the South Asian nation’s export earnings. It employs about 4 million workers and accounts for roughly 10% of economic output.
In a bid to defuse the crisis, the government on Nov 1 formed a six-member wage board to review workers’ demands, which have gained momentum amid persistent inflation and rising living costs.
Police said they used tear gas to disperse garment workers attempting to block roads in Dhaka after protesters hurled bricks and stones at officers. Unrest was also reported in Ashulia and Gazipur, two manufacturing hubs on the outskirts of the capital.
Police and industry officials said protesters set fire to a police vehicle and vandalised a number of factories.
A damaged police vehicle after a clash between police and garment workers in Gazipur, Bangladesh, on Nov 2.
The clashes follow the Nov 1 protests and factory closures, with workers continuing to demand higher wages and the resolution of employment grievances.
“Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages in the world,” said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation and a workers’ representative on the wage board.
“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers.”
Factory owners said the industry faces higher costs, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in the Middle East and slowing demand in key export markets.
Mahmud Hasan Khan, president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, said around 20 to 25 factories were vandalised during the unrest and the office of a leather goods factory was also attacked.
“If this continues and factories are repeatedly forced to shut, we will have no option but to invoke the ‘no work, no pay’ provision,” he said.
Police personnel detain a garment worker during a protest demanding higher minimum wages in Dhaka on Nov 2, 2026.
Home Affairs Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warned of robust action: “Those acting against workers’ interests under the guise of labour protests and attempting to destabilise the country will be dealt with firmly,” he said.
Selim Raihan, an economics professor at the University of Dhaka, said that workers’ demands were understandable given high inflation and said there could be further unrest.
However, a substantial wage increase could raise production costs, squeeze profit margins and weaken Bangladesh’s price competitiveness, he said.
“A phased wage adjustment, improved productivity and fairer pricing from international buyers are essential to balancing workers’ welfare with industrial sustainability,” he said. REUTERS

布拉格11月2日电 据CTK通讯社报道，布拉格一家法院周一裁定一名涉嫌在捷克共和国从事间谍活动的中国男子无罪，并下令释放他。

捷克媒体称杨是一家共产党下属报纸的记者，他被指控“为外国势力进行未经授权的活动”。
中国当局在评论六月一名捷克公民在中国被拘留一事时要求释放该男子。
中国官员称，这名捷克男子因涉嫌危害国家安全罪被中国拘留。

Czech court acquits and releases Chinese man accused of spying, news agency says
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Published Nov 03, 2026, 02:32 AM
Updated Nov 03, 2026, 02:32 AM
PRAGUE, Nov 2 - A Prague court ruled on Monday that a Chinese man suspected of espionage in the Czech Republic was not guilty and ordered his release, the news agency CTK reported.
The man, who had worked in Prague as a journalist, was arrested in January, accused of building up connections with Czech officials and collecting information that may be harmful to the Czech Republic.
But a court ruled that his activity was not criminal, CTK said.
A state attorney appealed both the ruling and the release from custody, sending the case to a higher court, CTK said. Yang Yiming, who had denied wrongdoing, was not ordered to remain in the country, but his lawyer said he was not planning to leave at the moment, it said.
Yang, who Czech media said was a reporter for a Communist Party-affiliated newspaper, had been charged with conducting "unauthorised activity for a foreign power".
Chinese authorities had demanded the release of the man while commenting on the June detention of a Czech citizen in China.
The Czech man has been held in China on suspicion of national security offences, Chinese officials said.
Czech Foreign Minister Petr Macinka has said the cases were unrelated.
Beijing and Prague have signalled a warming of diplomatic ties in recent months after tensions under the previous Czech administration due to its strong ties with Taiwan, the democratically governed island claimed by China.
The Czech government in power since last December has sought a more pragmatic relationship with Beijing. REUTERS
